description.narrative: P4I’s goal is to contribute to ‘quality infrastructure development that drives sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth in Southeast Asia’. The end-of-investment outcomes are ‘Southeast Asian agencies improve decision-making and practise towards quality infrastructure’ and ‘Strong partnerships among Australian and Southeast Asian government agencies and other institutions build regional commitment to quality infrastructure investment’. P4I focusses on the transport, energy, and telecommunications sectors, and integrates cross-cutting issues of climate change, gender equality and social inclusion.

description.narrative: Australia is supporting Laos to strengthen its capacity to manage climate and disaster risks across the transport sector. The National Contingency Plan for the Department of Roads, co-developed with Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I), is a cornerstone of Laos’ broader Integrated Multimodal Transport Strategy. ‍ P4I DRR specialists worked with the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) to co-develop the plan, ensuring it reflects practical stakeholder input, robust disaster risk analyses and scenario testing. Workshops then brought together national, provincial and district stakeholders to validate the plan, identify implementation priorities and to clarify roles and responsibilities. Simulation exercises and lessons-learned sessions with MPWT internalised contingency planning across departments and embedded DRR into transport governance systems. ‍ Australia is supporting Laos to have institutional tools, knowledge and partnerships to ensure the continuity and resilience of its transport sector to climate and disaster risks. This work supports an immediate project pipeline worth $212 million across Laos. ‍ The plan has already shaped the Integrated Multimodal Transport Strategy, embedding disaster preparedness and continuity planning into national frameworks.

description.narrative: Australia is supporting Thailand’s efforts to meet international climate commitments across its maritime sector. Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) is cooperating with the Marine Department and Port Authority of Thailand to identify pathways to reduce greenhouse gas emissions across ports, shipping and other maritime infrastructure, while promoting economic competitiveness, resilience and inclusivity. ‍ Cooperation with Thailand through P4I has produced policy and technical analyses on green shipping corridors and low-emissions port infrastructure including; a multi-criteria framework to evaluate the feasibility and impact of green shipping corridors; delivered training to Thai Government officials on the low-carbon transition; and taken steps to increase Thailand’s access to climate finance sources for emission reduction technologies and infrastructure upgrades. ‍ Through these efforts, Australia is supporting Thailand to deepen its knowledge, tools and institutional capacity to accelerate its transition to a low-emissions maritime sector, setting a benchmark for climate-smart infrastructure and fostering replicable models for green shipping corridors across the ASEAN region.

Building and Upgrading Cross-Border Facilities in Laos and Enhancing Laos' Regional Connectivity through the Laos Australia Connectivity Partnership ‍ As part of the Laos – Australia Connectivity Partnership, the Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) is providing support to the Government of Laos to build and upgrade two cross-border facilities along Laos’ National Road No.2. The facilities align with G20 principles for quality infrastructure through embedding climate resilience and disaster mitigation measures, such as landslide, earthquakes, flooding and fire protection, and low emission elements such as Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), solar panel roofs and electric vehicle (EV) charges within cross-border facility designs. Social inclusion principles were integrated, including suggestions on the enhanced participation of people with disabilities, ethnic minorities and women; enhancing physical accessibility – such as special parking areas and pedestrian ramps; and the provision of segregated male/female sanitary facilities.

Infrastructure development is a significant challenge in the Philippines which faces an estimated investment gap of USD69 billion. Australia is supporting the Philippines address challenges to close this gap through Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I). P4I is working with the Philippines Department of Transportation (DOTr) to help develop a robust transport infrastructure pipeline. This has included the joint development of a Rail Financial Performance Assessment Tool to improve the preparation and evaluation of rail projects in country. DOTr is actively integrating key performance indicators identified from the tool into ongoing and future Operations and Maintenance contracts for the North-South Commuter Railway and Metro Manila Subway. P4I included climate and disaster resilience metrics into the tool and has identified data gaps influencing DOTr capacity in utilizing these metrics. DOTr is now developing plans to strengthen data collection and capacity development plans to operationalize the metrics.

Laos faces significant energy transition challenges, including a surplus of hydropower generated energy due to grid constraints and a significant seasonal reliance on electricity imports. In parallel, Laos depends on fossil-fuel based fertiliser imports for its agricultural sector, presenting energy security risks and economic challenges for the country's development trajectory. ‍ Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I), with the Mekong Region Futures Institute and CSIRO, provided technical assistance to evaluate potential hydrogen and ammonia end-uses utilising the country’s surplus hydropower. This support enabled comprehensive techno-economic analysis and strategic planning with the Ministry of Energy and Mines (MEM) to develop a National Green Hydrogen and Ammonia Roadmap. The assistance included substantial workforce development initiatives: Master of Science electrochemistry curriculum at the National University of Laos, training-of-trainers programs for local lecturers, future internship placements for Lao students in Australia, and proposal for a centre of excellence to drive domestic research capacity. ‍ The roadmap was formally endorsed by MEM at a national workshop in September 2024, establishing Laos as one of the first Least Developed Countries with comprehensive green hydrogen planning. The framework provides pathways for immediate fertiliser production and long-term industrial applications.

description.narrative: Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) is supporting Cambodia to strengthen the resilience of its national road infrastructure to climate change. A partnership between the Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) and Austroads, facilitated by P4I, is working to integrate climate-responsive design into road standards and specifications. This includes green infrastructure solutions – such as infiltration systems to manage water – drawing on international best practice specifically adapted for Cambodia’s climate, soils and construction capabilities. Australia is also assisting Cambodia to update road inspection and maintenance standards and practices to ensure infrastructure is less vulnerable to extreme weather events. ‍ By embedding climate adaptation principles into national road design, construction, and maintenance practices, our partnership is increasing Cambodia’s resilience to flooding, stormwater impacts, and climate variability while strengthening MPWT’s capacity to contribute to Cambodia’s adaptation and resilience goals. These standards are already being incorporated into the design and procurement processes for Cambodia’s $2.4 billion road investment pipeline.

Requested by Cambodia's Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT), through Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I), Austroads has been assisting MPWT since late 2022 in reviewing and updating design standards and technical guidelines for resilient bridge and road infrastructure. To assist integration and promote inclusion, P4I supported the establishment of a technical working group on gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) at MPWT. This collaboration between P4I, Austroads and MPWT has formulated six technical specifications and an inclusive design principles checklist that integrates GEDSI considerations into the standards. The checklist probes whether projects have conducted a gender and inclusion analysis; consulted vulnerable and disability groups ahead of contracting; address mobility and accessibility needs and safety concerns for women, persons with disabilities, children and socially-excluded groups. One standard, the Pavement Design Specification, completed stakeholder consultations and has been translated into Khmer

Since 2022, Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) has partnered with Cambodia’s Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) to support the development of inclusive and resilient mobility infrastructure. P4I supported the revision of Cambodia’s road, bridge and associated infrastructure standards, which were last updated in the early 2000s and no longer cater to the country's rapid development, impacts from climate change and technological advancements. ‍ P4I facilitated engagement and collaboration between Austroads – the association of Australian transport agencies – and MPWT to support the revision and drafting of contemporary, fit-for-purpose and adaptable technical standards. This outcome enables MPWT to develop resilient road, bridge and associated infrastructure assets into the future. ‍ In 2024, P4I through Austroads finalised seven road, bridge and auxiliary standards and specifications which embed local geography – climate and topography – inclusion and resilience elements. The standards and specifications were formally adopted by the Royal Government of Cambodia in March 2025 during an official handover ceremony. The standards are already being incorporated into the design and procurement processes for Cambodia’s $2.4 billion road investment pipeline.

Since 2022, Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) has supported the ASEAN Secretariat to enhance the efficiency of shipping container processing. Through a collaborative study, the Asian Solidarity Economy Council (ASEC) developed an Implementation Framework and Action Plan for Enhancing Container Processing and Circulation which was formally adopted at the 28th ASEAN Transport Ministers Meeting. The Action Plan establishes specific strategies, actions, timelines and outcomes for enhancing container processing and circulation within ASEAN region. ‍ Two strategies in the Action Plan are the review and renewal of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) guidelines, regulations and implementation models for ports and relevant infrastructure, and the review of container port digitalisation and automation. ASEC invited P4I to collaborate and lead the drafting of ASEAN Port Sector PPP Guidelines and ASEAN Port Digitalisation and Automation Best Practice Study. ‍ Both reports were endorsed during the 30th ASEAN Transport Ministers Meeting held in November 2024. The reports cover port digitalisation and automation best practices, climate resilient port design, construction, maintenance and operations through port PPPs, with a view to introducing efficiency gains into port operations and crowd-in private financing of maritime infrastructure across ASEAN. This helps promote Australia’s regional engagement on these issues, building upon substantive bilateral engagements.

Since 2022, Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) has supported the Government of the Philippines to increase private sector infrastructure financing to address an estimated investment gap of $105 billion. P4I supported the amendment of Philippines Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Code (Republic Act 11966) in 2023 through technical advice to the PPP Center (PPPC) – a national government agency which serves as the central coordinating and monitoring agency for all PPP projects in the Philippines. ‍ In 2024, P4I continued to support PPPC to operationalise the Code by providing technical advice to draft the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), which took effect in April 2024. P4I worked with the PPPC to build GEDSI standards into the IRR, including the integration of key performance indicators, social metrics, broader representation into decision-making groups and project safeguards. The standards also mandate the representation of civil society organisations in the procurement processes of both local and national PPP project initiatives. ‍ As a result, the PPPC now applies these standards as inputs and references during the development of PPP policies, programs and recommendations for various government agencies in the Philippines.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted supply chains and exposed structural issues in the container industry. Through the Partnerships for Infrastructure program, and working with the ASEAN Secretariat and Thailand, Australia supported a rapid assessment of short-to-medium term actions that could help improve container circulation in Southeast Asia and assist economic recovery. The recommendations, including improving port capacity and hinterland connectivity, enhancing resilience of customs processes, and investigating potential container manufacturing in ASEAN, were used by the ASEAN Secretariat to develop an Implementation Framework adopted by ASEAN Transport Ministers in October 2022, demonstrating the value and practical impact of this support.

Under the umbrella of the Laos-Australia Connectivity Partnership, Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) collaborated with the Laos’ Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT) to strengthen transport and logistics connectivity policy and planning. Across 2024, P4I and MPWT co-developed an Integrated Multimodal National Transport Strategy (NTS) for Laos that promotes evidence-based decision-making in transport policy and projects. The co-development process also included targeted capacity building of MPWT staff in transport strategy development and implementation. ‍ The NTS was finalised in October 2024 and provides the foundation for building a viable, integrated, resilient and inclusive multimodal transport network in Laos, with a view to make it financially and economically sustainable, supporting passenger and freight operations and promoting national social and economic development. The NTS will inform an immediate project pipeline worth $212 million. ‍ The NTS and capacity building informed a Five Northern Provinces Strategic Plan for transport that provides the template for the preparation of the northern, central and southern strategic transport plans and informed the Government of Laos’ five-year 10th National and Social Economic Development Plan and MPWT’s 5 Year Development Plan. This is expected to be adopted as an official MPWT policy by end 2025.

With its strategic location on the Malacca Strait, Malaysia is well placed to become a Southeast Asian hub to supply the green fuel services (‘green bunkering’) needed to decarbonise shipping. Australia’s collaboration with Malaysia through Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) has highlighted this potential and is supporting key policy outcomes. P4I’s feasibility study on the potential for Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) to become a green bunkering hub informed the Malaysian Government’s August 2023 National Energy Transition Roadmap. The Roadmap sets the goal of establishing Malaysia as a green bunkering hub, with a new taskforce created to help achieve this. It commits to unlock market opportunities for future fuels and proposes a 40% target for low-carbon fuel penetration in marine transport by 2050. As part of this activity, P4I also supported the Port of Melbourne to share work on green shipping with partners.

Women remain significantly under-represented across Southeast Asia's infrastructure workforce, accounting for 14% and 8% of transport and energy sector positions respectively. These roles are concentrated in low-tier administrative rather than technical positions, with career advancement often constrained by systemic barriers including limited access to upskilling, networking opportunities and senior role models. ‍ In partnership with the Techo Sen Institute (TSI) and the University of Melbourne’s (UoM) Women in Transport Leadership Knowledge Network, P4I delivered targeted capacity building on gender equality and leadership to 61 officers at Cambodia’s Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MPWT), including 42 women. The initiative also established mentorship connections between 13 MPWT officers and senior Australian transport executives. ‍ Mentees reported enhanced leadership confidence and communication capabilities, resulting in tangible career advancement including one promotion from Deputy Director to Director and one Australian secondment application. With UoM support, TSI is looking to integrate the capacity building component into one of their Bachelor programs, potentially reaching 150 students annually.
